author: Doctor
text:
fx7877, look on the weekly chart and see where we are. Do you spot old demand?...if so, does it not make sense for price to now rise and build a bullish market?...there is more upside left in this move due to much more attractive (profit) laying there for the taking higher up on the weekly chart. While it unfolds you must check the monthly candle at the start of each new month to be aware of what is going on there.

If we are turning bullish, why would we see supply coming off old supply areas on the way down into major monhly demand, this is one of the reasons I marked the chart with invert. When we hit old supply on the way up, your logic needs to become inverted, old supply in a bullish market will likely give us pullbacks, but no return to the down side. The move up must first establish itself and you the individual trader have to develop your own means to determine when this has happened. It will become part of your risk appetite and available.

The old supply areas on the way up tend to make nice places where we gain support, and yes for those reading carefully this gels with my thoughts on support/demand and resistance supply. Where you change this in when the market changes sentiment and eventually direction. Make sense?

Letting this play out in areas where now are will teach a lot of people patience as you must come to expect a lot of volatile price action when the next leg is developing. Deep moves down on lower time frames are just that, they dont show as clarity on the upper time frames where you should be looking for signals.

If this is hurting your head, take two aspirin and call me in the morning:)

author: Doctor
text:
If we are bullish and I see these pullbacks, I will take a long off support as long as price action is with me and it shows a clear sign of buying. If price were to fall to the beginning of the last up leg, I will again look for price action there if it gains support and we already know its an area where there was buying in the past. Correct of price building a base on a lower time frame, it will look like a drift down until it finds support...if support fails it will drop off more sharply due to bears coming in. At that point I would wait for a pull back up into the area we wanted to see support, but was just broken therefore it is now resistance and we enter short on a failed break above that and with price action guiding us.

All simple with nothing to cloud our decisions and there are no bets, this is trading, not gambling!

author: Doctor
text:
It has been a while since I posted a trade, so here is a live one. This is Brent crude on the daily time frame.

Overhead we have a gray box that is an old supply area, we touched the bottom of this box four days ago and I waited for a deeper push into the box. Clearly we didnt get a deeper push in and I had to sit and wait for the next area to be hit lower down and where some S/R and price action would bring a trade.

If you look at candle A, you will see it pinned old supply and the market rose as expected. But what does the close of that candle tell you?....look at its close in context to what history is around it, it is at the same price as the previous bullish move up. Pure fluke you say, yeah sure!

The following day we see a false bullish move which on the intraday charts would have had day traders going long. I had no intention of going long when pro money had already signaled their intentions. It was the break of the 2nd last candle today that got me in short. The entry was taken off the 15min chart as it tends to be a little easier to get entries with oil, rather than the 5min which can easily mess you about. If you look at your own 4hr chart you will see a large spike down, this was the candle that got my attention, note it pinned old supply. On the 1hr the same area has two candles with long tails and no bullish follow through, if you saw that and went long. Bad move, it was not a supply demand play at all. The overall market picture must be in your mind at all times and not focus purely on supply and demand intra day. The higher time frame price action and their supply and demand areas take priority.

Walking down from where I entered I have a number of choices for a target. I can go for the last demand area which is pretty much hit now, or go lower to my blue line which is the most significant S/R on the chart and an obvious place as I like to see. Or I can sit through the pain of the ugly decision area which is a real messy price action area, but if broken there is only place left to go ad that is 90usd or less. Do keep in mind my blue S/R line did see strong bullish move off back in Dec 2011. A reaction there is highly likely, but equally likely not to turn the market back above 118 unless the bulls manage to get a ton of orders.

There is the possibility we are at the beginning of a bear oil market. We need a lot more information before taking longer term bearish trades. A few weeks of bearish price action would suit my view of the market, then wait for weekly and monthly candles to tell us more. If you played this move intra day, it is now over. And you wait again.

author: Doctor
text:
first up is a 4hr chart of the euro/usd.

We have been in bullish mode for a while now, and here is a deeper look into the price structure. The lower small black line is the origin of the move, there was no way anyone other that those who bought at the last bullish candle that pinned support would have been in that move, the break above and retest of resistance which then became support was also a near impossible move to be in. note the nice clean price action as each new bullish candle formed and the lack of any pullback as price moved up. Price was certainly on a mission here and looking to get some where.

The two upper black lines are here to show you how the candle tails removed quickly old demand, a nice trick if you can spot this in real time and is an S/R play when you break it down. Marker E shows the clean price action and the desire of the bulls to get price higher.

My lower blue line is the last place I see on the 4hr where the bulls and have any chance of taking this back. Even in the very recent past, only the previous two candles showed strength to the bears. Given we have a wall of buyers that were left by the side of the road at E, would you short this?....all those buyers need to be absorbed if the market is going to turn and a show of strength by the bears.

Now down to the 1hr where it gets interesting, or perhaps more interesting from an intra day perspective.

Lower box is a consolidation of price and so too is the box above, look at your own 1hr chart with nothing but candles on there, can you see this by eye?....if you can, you have developed a good edge over other traders who look for breaks rather than how and where the move developed etc. Now look at C, again can you see these candles touch the top of old resistance/new support/new demand and in doing so they quickly fill new demand and race off, none of us would have caught these moves even on the 1hr. Again, the bulls wanted price higher, fast!

At the top of the chart we have a minor S/R level. This was the area I was looking at for the past few days while putting my comments in this part of the forum. We have broken below it and retested old support, which at A was bullish activity rejected and the bears ran with it, no surprise there as it was classic S/R at work, but no way would I take it. This is still short term bearish trading and not for me, too risky.

Again we try to test old support a second time which has already once before proved to be resistance and the remaining bulls didnt have the necessary $$ to push price above and only one thing then will happen, price falls off.

The last attempts by the bulls are both candles marked at B. Note the bearish move down is rather weak looking on the 1hr, but strong on the 4hr. Now note the time, this happened in the Asian session where it is typically quiet.

Now what?......we wait for a reaction off an area where we can see old bulls active, or you trade it lower with the greatest of care because we have strong bullish history not far from where price is at the moment. Market sentiment doesnt change direction on a dime.

D is one place I will carefully watch, after that it would be my blue line on the 4hr chart.

You cant force a trade, so let the price come to your pre planned area and where you have a better opportunity of reducing your risk and getting points in the bank. The daily is starting to suggest me fall to my 4hr blue line, we wait for a close before taking that decision. If this means a failure for bullish activity around D, I will skip the euro and look at something else until next week. Why?....because if no bullish activity happens soon, we will likely close on a strong bearish weekly candle and I wont stand in the way of a raging bear!

Enjoy!

author: Doctor
text:
Simon, even trading intraday you need to look at where price has been and where it is next going to show a high probability of a reaction. Now this next statement is not to be taken as trading advice....we are coming down with scalpers shorting the euro, we know this because there is no sign of pro money behind the move or else price action would not look so chaotic.

I do expect a bounce somewhere soon, we are not far from old demand, and the demand was very strong. What messes up an otherwise nice picture is the long wave candle prior to the demand candle as seen on the hourly chart.

Current price action on the 15min shows buying and a base being built which may act as support. We just dont know yet if the bulls will run with this early or price consolidate and mess us about intraday for a while longer.

In 30mins time we have a 4hr candle forming and it has a tiny body so far and a mildly bearish outlook. It is forming, so this is not yet factual information.

Personally I would like a see a push deeper and then the bulls take over. If we break lower I will wait for a solid retest of old support to see will it act as resistance before shorting, and even then I will keep a tight stop and lower target points count.

author: Doctor
text:
Simon, a follow up on what I posted earlier on the euro.

We reached the D candle I mentioned and got some real choppy price action as a reaction from this level. Given we were getting into the NY session I generally do no expect a lot to happen then. Right now we have just seen price poke its head above a range it has formed and waiting for the bulls to run with this. If they take it we have nice support below and will be useful to watch. Further up and to the left candle D 1hr you will see a small cluster of candles which is our next area of resistance. This also shows up closer to current price in the form of a bearish sell off which we are now eating our way through. This is bullish strength and a sign pro money active. Note the 5min and 15min tails.

I will post a chart tomorrow if I can get some clarity onto my charts and let some additional history become a useful educational tool. Otherwise it is speculation and I'd rather people make up their own minds and get used to conducting their own analysis.

The old fable about giving a man a fish etc.
